native_retrieval.title: Jharkhand govt to launch model agriculture villages and panchayats - The Times of India
native_retrieval.snippet: Ranchi: The Jharkhand govt would design model agriculture villages and panchayats across the state to ensure targeted implementation of welfare schemes based on local requirements rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.Reviewing the agriculture department’s plans, chief minister (CM) Hemant Soren on Friday directed the department to identify villages or panchayats in every district for the initiative and conduct detailed surveys to assess the needs of farmers before rolling out govt programmes/ welfare schemes.He stressed the need for direct engagement with farmers and addressing key infrastructure gaps, including soil testing facilities and irrigation systems. “Govt interventions should be guided by ground realities to maximise benefits for the farming community,” he said.Talking to STOI, agriculture minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said, “The project aims to create clusters of villages, where farming, fisheries or animal husbandry schemes can be implemented in a coordinated manner after assessing local needs instead of randomly applying schemes so that the maximum number of people are benefitted.”The pilot project will initially focus on areas with large tracts of fallow or uncultivated land.

native_retrieval.title: Ford Closes 113-Year-Old Assembly Line to Speed Up Production of a $30000 Electric Truck - Fingerlakes1.com
native_retrieval.snippet: Home » Life » Automotive » Ford Closes 113-Year-Old Assembly Line to Speed Up Production of a $30000 Electric Truck. # Ford Closes 113-Year-Old Assembly Line to Speed Up Production of a $30000 Electric Truck. Ford is preparing one of the biggest manufacturing changes in its modern history as it develops an affordable midsize electric pickup for 2027. ### Ford Universal EV Production System. The Ford Universal EV Production System replaces one long moving conveyor with what the company calls an “assembly tree.” Three major sections of the truck will be built at the same time on separate lines before being joined together. Ford says this layout could make the truck’s assembly process up to 40 percent faster than that of the vehicles currently built at the Louisville Assembly Plant. Ford’s new electric truck will be the first vehicle built on its Universal EV Platform. Its wiring harness is also expected to be more than 4,000 feet shorter than the system used in Ford’s first-generation electric SUV.

native_retrieval.title: Agriculture students at loggerheads with govt over AO, AAO recruitment - Deccan Herald
native_retrieval.snippet: Agriculture students at loggerheads with govt over AO, AAO recruitmentStudents under the banner of the Agriculture Degree Students’ Association have been staging protests across agricultural universities in the state. Dharwad/Shivamogga: With less than three weeks left for the Karnataka Examinations Authority’s (KEA) recruitment examination for Agriculture Officer (AO) and Assistant Agriculture Officer (AAO) posts, students of the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad, have intensified their protest, demanding that the state government withdraw the recruitment notification and issue a fresh one. The government has notified recruitment for 945 Group-B AO and AAO posts in the Agriculture Department, with the examination scheduled for August 8 and 9. However, the inclusion of BE Biotechnology graduates and students from private agriculture colleges among the eligible candidates has sparked widespread opposition from agriculture students, who argue that the technical posts should be reserved exclusively for graduates with agriculture and allied agriculture degrees. Students under the banner of the Agriculture Degree Students’ Association have been staging protests across agricultural universities in the state.

english_retrieval.title: Sheikh Hasina ally to step down as Bangladesh's president - BBC
english_retrieval.snippet: # Sheikh Hasina ally to step down as Bangladesh's president. Bangladesh president Mohammed Shahabuddin is set to resign, as concerns grow that his former ally, ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, will return to the country. Shahabuddin's resignation comes days after Hasina told Reuters that she would return to Bangladesh, where she faces the death penalty for crushing student-led protests in 2024 which led to the toppling of her government. Since then, Shahabuddin has been under pressure to resign from leaders of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party, sources tell BBC Bangla. A senior official told BBC Bangla that Shahabuddin would tender his resignation to the parliament speaker, who returns to Bangladesh on Friday. Shahabuddin's spokesperson also told Reuters the president, who been in his role since 2023, is expected to quit on Friday. Earlier this month, Hasina said in a Reuters interview that she and her allies would return from exile in India and face the court in Bangladesh.

english_retrieval.snippet: Asia Pacific|Bangladesh’s President Resigns Amid Uncertainty Over Ex-Leader’s Plans. You have a preview view of this article while we are checking your access. # Bangladesh’s President Resigns Amid Uncertainty Over Ex-Leader’s Plans. President Mohammed Shahabuddin stepped down as speculation swirled over the possible return of his onetime ally Sheikh Hasina, who was ousted as prime minister and fled to India. President Mohammed Shahabuddin of Bangladesh resigned on Fridayas Bangladeshis anticipated the return and surrender of the ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, his onetime ally who fled to India before being convicted of crimes against humanity last year. Mr. Shahabuddin, 76, who was halfway into his term in the largely ceremonial post of president, cited illnessas the reason for his resignation. Mr. Shahabuddin’s resignation comes only weeks after Ms. Hasina announced in an interview with Reuters that she planned to return to Bangladesh in December to face the charges against her, which she denies.
